Photograph: China News Service/Getty Images China Typhoon Narra: record flood waters submerge homes and force mass evacuations in China Heavy rain expected in parts of Vietnam and southern ‌China, as another storm system, Typhoon Saudel, heads for Japan and Taiwan Reuters Tue 25 Aug 2026 21.46 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google Widespread flooding triggered by Typhoon Narra has submerged homes and forced mass evacuations in southern China, as another storm system tracked towards Japan and Taiwan . Authorities in Chongzuo, in China’s Guangxi region – famous for its giant waterfalls and karst limestone mountains – on Tuesday evacuated more than 15,000 people after water ⁠levels surpassed a record high set in 2008. Rising flood waters have prompted China to relocate a total of 54,000 people in Guangxi, state television said. Narra made landfall as a tropical storm on Tuesday evening ⁠in China’s southern island province of Hainan after lingering over the Beibu Gulf for ‌several days, dumping heavy rain on ‌Guangxi, Hainan and Guangdong. Heavy rain is expected to persist across parts of Vietnam and southern ‌China through Wednesday, with areas of Guangxi, Guangdong, Hainan and Fujian forecast to receive torrential rain, state media said. 0:53 Typhoon Narra floods cities in China’s Guangxi region – video In Chongzuo, river water overflowed into the city, with water levels reaching the rooftops of some buildings and power lines. A notice from Chongzuo authorities on Monday ordered all businesses and tourist operations to cease and urged evacuated residents not to return to high-risk areas. Meanwhile, medium-strength Typhoon Saudel moved towards southern Japan and northern Taiwan where ‌it is expected to bring sporadic heavy rain, as Taiwan reported one dead and four missing from a separate weather system over its south and east. Japan’s weather agency warned of destructive winds and high seas as Typhoon Saudel approached the south-western islands of Okinawa prefecture. Saudel is expected to pass to the north of Taiwan starting late Thursday and into Friday, though its intensity is forecast to gradually weaken, the island’s Central Weather Administration said. View image in fullscreen A resident wearing a raincoat wades through flood water inside an inundated home in Zihguan District, Kaohsiung, Taiwan. Photograph: Cheng-Chia Huang/ZUMA Press Wire/Shutterstock However, there is uncertainty about ⁠the timing and extent of the typhoon’s rainfall impact, it added. In southern and eastern Taiwan, ​the government reported one person dead and ​four missing from a tropical depression ​that brought flooding in the cities of Tainan and Kaohsiung, home to more than 4 million people. During ​the three days from ‌Sunday to Tuesday, almost ​a metre (3.9 feet) of ​rain fell in Kaohsiung, which the government said exceeded rainfall during 2009’s devastating Typhoon Morakot that killed about 700 people and caused damage of up to $3bn. Saudel is forecast to hit the coast in the south-eastern Chinese province of Fujian from late Thursday to early Friday. https://www.dw.com/en/russian-foreign-mi.text: Skip to content Skip to main menu Skip to more DW sites https://p.dw.com/p/5PM69 Prefer DW on Google Alexander Darchiev was appointed ambassador to the US after Donald Trump returned to the White House Image: Russian Foreign Ministry/Avalon/Photoshot/picture alliance Advertisement Russia's Foreign Ministry said Wednesday that Alexander Darchiev, Moscow's ambassador to the US , died from an unspecified chronic illness in Moscow at the age of 66. Darchiev was appointed to the post by Russian President Vladimir Putin in March 2025 after Donald Trump returned to the White House and the two countries sought to improve relations. The post had been vacant for six months before his appointment after hardliner Anatoly Antonov was relieved of his duties in October 2024. In a statement, Foreign Ministry spokeswoman Maria Zakharova described Darchiev as "an outstanding diplomat, experienced leader, good comrade and mentor" and a brilliant scholar on US history and affairs. What was Russia's ambassador to US known for? Zakharova warned against the spread of conspiracy theories surrounding Darchiev's passing, accusing US media outlets of being "particularly active" in that regard. Darchiev, known for his public denunciations of the West, had previously led the Foreign Ministry's North America and North Atlantic departments and served as ambassador to Canada from 2014 to 2021. He also led Russia's negotiating team during February 2025 Ukraine peace talks with the US in Istanbul, Turkey. No date has been given for his funeral. Details for a memorial service will be announced at a later date, Zakharova said.
